correctness.rationale: An independent operational-time check uses the renewal equation at the first Poisson redraw: the projection's characteristic-function Laplace transform is A/(1−αA), where A=E[(w+α−ikvY)⁻¹] and Y is the initial directional projection. Expansion at k=0 with μ₂=1/d and μ₄=3/[d(d+2)] gives the recorded transforms, with the fourth coefficient including both the single-direction μ₄ and repeated-direction αμ₂² terms. The independent inverse clock inserts s^ν for w and multiplies by s^(ν−1). With no redraw the operational jth even moment starts at v^j μ_j u^j; the redraw error is O(u^(j+1)) as u↓0. The poles at zero of the operational transforms give growth 2v²μ₂ u/α and 12v⁴μ₂² u²/α², with polynomially bounded remainders of orders 1 and u+1. Averaging using E[(E_ν(t))^j]=j!t^(jν)/Γ(1+jν) justifies both kurtosis limits without a Laplace-to-pointwise inference. Continuity follows also from the marginal clock scaling and the bound on displacement; the no-redraw event gives positive variance for positive t. Digamma monotonicity gives the unique short-time boundary and strict late positivity for 0<ν<1; the intermediate value theorem yields at least one finite zero for ν>ν_d. The derivative F′(1)=14 verifies the large-d expansion; an independent numerical bisection gives ν₂≈0.693572909926177. Redraw rate α means flip rate α/2 in d=1. No uniqueness, global positivity below threshold or sign at equality is inferred. The supplied check.py was inspected, not executed.
